- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if 10-day average is > 75% of 30-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.20 → -0.10 → +0.20), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
